clue.text: Sort of dress said to restrain a disciplinarian?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a dress with no shoulder straps
second meaning, read as two words: '...!', the plea you would make to someone too fond of the strap

explanation.surface: A puzzling question about a type of garment somehow being told to curb a strict teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into STRAP LESS and it becomes an order to a teacher who beats pupils with a leather strap: use it less.
explanation.definitionFit: A dress without shoulder straps is the standard fashion term for a bare-shouldered gown.

clue.text: Pitch spread in piles

indicators.note: spread suggests the letters are scattered and laid out afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: Something tossed and scattered among heaps, like hay on a farm.
explanation.definitionFit: A sales pitch is a practised patter, which is exactly what this borrowed German word for a glib talk means.

clue.text: List includes Independent Party

indicators.note: includes says the list word takes the next piece inside it

parts.note: a roster is a list of names on duty
I is the standard abbreviation for Independent, as in election results

explanation.surface: A candidates' list containing an independent alongside a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' looks like a political noun, but here it is the verb: to make merry noisily.
explanation.definitionFit: To roister is to revel boisterously, which is partying in the verb sense.

clue.text: Pound back on hot dog

indicators.note: on places the next piece after the first in a down clue's run
back tells you to read the word for pound in reverse order

parts.note: a pound is an enclosure for animals, as is a coop
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A hot dog sold at a price of one pound, maybe at the back of a stall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot dog' reads as a sausage in a bun, but the clue splits it: 'hot' gives H and 'dog' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pooch is an informal, affectionate word for a pet hound.

clue.text: Losing hair, Uriah Heep's playing southern city of old

indicators.note: Losing says the letters of the next word must be taken away from the fodder
playing suggests the remaining letters are rearranged as if performed anew

parts.note: taken as written, its letters removed from the name

explanation.surface: Uriah Heep, Dickens's creepy clerk, or the rock band of that name, going bald while performing.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of HAIR out of URIAHHEEPS to leave UEEPHS, rearrange them as EPHESU, then add S for southern.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephesus was an ancient Greek city in Asia Minor, famous for its Temple of Artemis.

clue.text: Bank management furniture

parts.note: a river bank is its side
the board is a company's management

explanation.surface: A bank's managers worried about office furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A sideboard is a piece of dining-room furniture with cupboards and drawers.

clue.text: Is a consumer jailed without society?

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the jail phrase sits outside the letter for society

parts.note: to be put away is to be locked up in prison

explanation.surface: A question whether a shopper got locked up because they were cut off from society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' is the old sense of outside, not the modern lacking, so the jail phrase is wrapped round the society letter rather than shorn of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To put away food or drink is an idiom for eating or drinking a lot of it, i.e. consuming.

clue.text: Underwear that is contributing to heavy breathing

indicators.note: contributing to suggests the abbreviation is put into the breathing word

parts.note: pants as a noun plural means gasps, heavy breathing
i.e. is the Latin abbreviation id est, that is

explanation.surface: A cheeky line about lingerie that gets someone breathing hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Panties are women's or girls' knickers, an item of underwear.

clue.text: Maybe spreadsheet user thanks innovative Labour technology head

parts.note: ta is informal British for thanks

indicators.note: innovative suggests the letters are made new, rearranged into a fresh order
head picks out the first letter of technology

explanation.surface: A spreadsheet user thanking an inventive Labour party chief of technology.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabulator sets out data in tables, so a person working in a spreadsheet is one example.

clue.text: Old German's attempt to interrupt call by hospital

indicators.note: by places the hospital letter next to the rest, at the end
to interrupt says the attempt word breaks into the call word

parts.note: to call on someone is to visit them
a go is an attempt
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A German making an attempt to cut in on a hospital visit.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Visigoths were the western branch of the Goths, a Germanic people of late antiquity.

clue.text: Beaune, not the ultimate in wine, drunk with date and flowing water

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters are reeling into a new order
not the ultimate in says the last letter of wine is subtracted

explanation.surface: A bottle of Beaune, a Burgundy red, being drunk on a dinner date.
explanation.walkthrough: Take E (the end of wine) from BEAUNE plus D, leaving BAUND, and rearrange those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Danube is a major European river, so flowing water is a whimsical description of it.

clue.text: Brood that might be disengaged

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a set of eggs or chicks hatched together
second meaning: the pedal in a car that a driver engages and disengages

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition plays on cars: a clutch is engaged or disengaged to change gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A clutch is a nest of eggs or chicks, and also the mechanism linking engine and gearbox in a car.

clue.text: Employ information technology in low-key, on-screen assistance

indicators.note: Employ asks you to put the tech abbreviation to use within the next word
in says the tech letters go inside the low-key word

parts.note: subtle means understated, low-key

explanation.surface: Advice to use computers discreetly in giving help on screen.
explanation.definitionFit: Subtitles are captions that help viewers follow dialogue in a film or programme.

clue.text: Disease makes son shapely

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son, as in genealogies
curvy means shapely

explanation.surface: An illness that leaves a boy with a fine figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Scurvy is the vitamin C deficiency illness once common among sailors.

clue.text: Irish town's company provides assistance to wine drinker?

parts.note: Cork is a city in Ireland, here with its possessive s
a crew is a company, as of a ship

explanation.surface: A firm in an Irish town helping out someone fond of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A corkscrew helps someone who wants to drink wine by pulling the bottle's cork; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: Wagging tongues in your heartless youth

indicators.note: in says the shuffled tongues go inside the shortened your
heartless removes the middle pair of letters of your
wagging suggests the letters moving about into a new order

explanation.surface: Gossiping tongues around a callous young person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' removes the two middle letters of the four-letter word, leaving just its outer pair as the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A youngster is a young person, a youth.

clue.text: Shortage of boxes? Shame, but no pressure

parts.note: to box is to spar, so boxes is spars

indicators.note: but no says the pressure letter is left out of the word for shame

parts.note: 'what a shame' and 'what a pity' mean the same
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A lament about too few boxes, though nobody felt any strain over it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxes' looks like containers, but it is the verb for fighting with fists: spars.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparsity means thinness or scarcity, so a lack or shortage.

clue.text: Bullying has journalists convinced to drop leader

parts.note: the press is journalists collectively

indicators.note: to drop leader means the first letter of the word for convinced goes

parts.note: to be sure is to be convinced

explanation.surface: Reporters intimidating someone into ousting their boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressure in the sense of coercion or intimidation is a form of bullying.

clue.text: Wet person in debt included in cast

indicators.note: included in says the debtor word sits inside the cast word

parts.note: to shy is to throw or cast
an ower is one who owes

explanation.surface: A feeble debtor among the actors of a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' suggests actors, but it is the verb throw, giving SHY.
explanation.definitionFit: Showery weather brings repeated brief rain, so it is wet.

clue.text: Course initially falls short in banqueting

indicators.note: short says that letter is missing from the feasting word

parts.note: banqueting is feasting

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letter of falls

explanation.surface: A meal's course falling short at a banquet.
explanation.definitionFit: An easting is a ship's course or distance made towards the east, a navigation term.

clue.text: To some extent includes cryptic spot

indicators.note: To some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cryptic clue partly containing a place.
explanation.definitionFit: To descry is a literary verb meaning to catch sight of, to spot.

clue.text: Wind is getting up — fabulous flyer needs company

indicators.note: getting up in a down clue means the word is read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: the roc is a giant bird of fable, as in the Arabian Nights

explanation.surface: Wind is rising and a mythical bird wants companions.
explanation.definitionFit: The sirocco is a hot wind blowing from North Africa across the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Provided glass on a mobile

indicators.note: mobile means moving about, so the letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: Supplied a glass for a mobile phone, or a drink while on the move.
explanation.definitionFit: As long as is a conjunction meaning on condition that, which is what provided means.

clue.text: Bear out of honey finally, after changing fiver

indicators.note: after places the final letter of honey at the end
changing says the letters of fiver are altered into a new order
finally picks out the last letter of honey

explanation.surface: A bear going out for honey after getting change for a five-pound note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear out' looks like a bear leaving, but it is the phrasal verb meaning confirm.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear out a claim is to confirm or support it, an idiom for proving true.

clue.text: Senior Tory leaders getting in by means of Panorama

indicators.note: getting in says those first letters go inside the word for by means of

parts.note: via means by means of

indicators.note: leaders picks out the first letters of Senior and Tory

explanation.surface: Top Conservatives appearing on the BBC current-affairs programme Panorama.
explanation.definitionFit: A vista is a broad view, a sweeping scene, just as a panorama is.

clue.text: Rival holding back Greek fashion

indicators.note: holding says the enemy word wraps round the reversed abbreviation

parts.note: a foe is an opponent or rival

indicators.note: back says the Greek abbreviation is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A competitor restraining the return of Greek fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: To forge something is to shape or make it, which is fashioning it.

clue.text: Drive time around noon — can't wait!

indicators.note: around says the drive and time letters surround the noon letter

parts.note: an urge is a drive or impulse

explanation.surface: Someone impatient to drive off at midday.
explanation.definitionFit: Something urgent demands immediate attention, so it cannot be put off.

clue.text: Fast current at the start makes you anxious

indicators.note: at the start places the current word before the fast word

parts.note: in means fashionable or current
fast, as in held fast, means firmly fixed or secure

explanation.surface: A strong current at the start of a swim makes you nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like water flow, but it means fashionable: IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Insecure means lacking confidence or feeling unsure of oneself, so anxious.

clue.text: See 6
A girl more suited for performance

indicators.note: suited suggests the letters are made to fit a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A girl better cut out for acting.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigmarole is a lengthy, tiresome procedure, in the informal sense of a performance or palaver.
